header.reason: Kestrel moved its international half to Adyen after a country-by-country test on its own traffic. Elena calls it decided early, but we offered averages and our useful country analysis came weeks late.

findings.label: What started it
findings.finding: Lead with declines by country, the first thing Stefan checked.
findings.why: Stefan, Kestrel's first head of payments, started by pulling declines by country and saw weak international markets.
findings.quote: the first thing he did was pull declines by country

findings.label: Who decided
findings.finding: Give the CFO a number for his own business, not an average.

line.text: Authorization Boost increases acceptance rates by 3.8% on average

findings.why: Stefan recommended the move and the CFO approved it. Stefan needed a figure he could defend there.
findings.quote: I can't take an average to my CFO.

findings.label: The competitor
findings.finding: Explain where we stand on 'local acquiring', country by country.
findings.why: After Adyen's test, Stefan asked about approval rates by country, card type and issuer. Elena had no answer.
findings.quote: The phrase he kept using was 'local acquiring.'

findings.label: Our message
findings.finding: Stop leading with the average uplift claim.

line.text: Authorization Boost increases acceptance rates by 3.8% on average

findings.why: Stefan pushed back on the average uplift, and Elena says the number got silence.

findings.label: Missing proof
findings.finding: Show a market-by-market view of the customer's own approvals, with reasons.
findings.why: Our analysis had fixable findings and Stefan called it most useful, but it arrived after Adyen's test.
findings.quote: A market-by-market view of their own approval rates, with reasons.

findings.label: Their words
findings.finding: Say 'approvals' and 'money left on the table', not 'authorization'.

line.text: Authorization Boost increases acceptance rates by 3.8% on average

findings.why: Stefan described his problem as lost money and says 'approvals', never our word 'authorization'.
